window_input_group.description: All rates are per EA (each window unit). Rates are provided as fixed_time_minutes per EA, with size-bucket variants (S/M/L) for tasks where time varies significantly by window size. Window type modifier (FAC_XWIN_WINDOW_TYPE) is the PRIMARY cost driver within each size bucket. Muntin type modifier (FAC_XWIN_MUNTIN) is the SECONDARY cost driver. Base rates assume casement window type at medium size bucket, no muntins (none/GBG), brush application.

task_production_rates.name: Glass Masking — Tape and Film Method

S.notes: Small single-lite window. Tape edge + HDPE film. ~0.10 hrs.

M.notes: Medium window. More glass perimeter to tape. ~0.17 hrs.

L.notes: Large window. Extended perimeter. Secure film against wind. ~0.30 hrs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: UV-resistant tape at glass-to-frame edge, fine-line tape at 1/16 inch glass lap line, HDPE static-cling film over pane. Secondary tape to prevent film flutter from wind. Default method for Low-E glass (most NC windows) and standard single-lite/SDL/GBG windows. Research: 0.08-0.12 hrs/EA for single-lite medium window.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete glass coverage. Fine-line tape at lap line. Film secured.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete glass coverage. Precision fine-line tape. Verify seal at all tape edges.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. Premium fine-line tape for razor-sharp lap line. Double-check all edges.

task_production_rates.name: Glass Masking — Liquid Mask Method (TDL Non-Low-E Only)

S.notes: Small TDL. Brush-apply liquid mask per pane. ~0.20 hrs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply liquid masking product (Jasco Mask & Peel) to each individual glass pane. Faster than tape-and-film on multi-lite TDL windows. PROHIBITED on Low-E glass. Research: 0.20-0.50 hrs/EA for TDL masking depending on lite count.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Heavy, even application over each pane. Full cure before painting.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Heavy, even application. Full cure. Verify coverage completeness.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Heavy, even application. Full cure. Complete pane coverage verified.

task_production_rates.name: Glass Masking — Tape and Film for TDL (Low-E or Preference)

S.notes: Small TDL Low-E. Per-pane tape+film. ~0.30 hrs.

M.notes: Medium TDL Low-E. More panes to individually mask. ~0.50 hrs.

L.notes: Large TDL Low-E. Many individual pane masks. ~0.75 hrs. Highest masking labor.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Individually mask each glass pane in TDL window with tape at each muntin bar edge, then film per pane. Required for Low-E TDL where liquid mask is prohibited. Highest masking labor configuration. Research: 0.30-0.75 hrs/EA depending on lite count and size.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Each pane individually masked. Tape sealed at muntin bar edges.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Each pane masked. Fine-line tape at 1/16 inch glass lap on each lite.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Each pane masked. Premium fine-line tape. Perfect edge definition on every lite.

task_production_rates.name: Window Hardware Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all operable window hardware: locks, lifts, sash pulls, crank handles. Place in labeled ziplock bag. ~8 min per window. Simpler than door hardware (fewer pieces). Research: 0.10-0.20 hrs/EA (6-12 min). Fixed windows: skip entirely.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All hardware removed. Labeled bag per window.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All hardware removed. Labeled bag. Photographed.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All hardware removed. Labeled bag with detail photos. Alignment marks documented.

task_production_rates.name: Weatherstrip Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Protect weatherstripping from paint contact. Friction-fit: pull out and store. Non-removable: push low-tack tape deep into gap. ~8 min per operable window. Research: 0.10-0.15 hrs/EA (6-9 min). NEVER paint weatherstripping. Fixed windows: skip.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Stripping fully protected or removed. No paint contact risk.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Stripping protected/removed. Verified before prime/finish.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Stripping protected/removed. Verified and documented. Zero paint contact risk.

task_production_rates.name: Exterior Sill Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply tape and paper/film over finished exterior sill. ~4 min per window. Conditional on sill being already finished. Simple tape-and-paper application.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete sill coverage. Secure tape edges.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete sill coverage. Tape sealed at edges against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete sill coverage. Taped and sealed. Verified.

task_production_rates.name: Adjacent Casing Edge Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Light tape at casing-to-frame junction when casing is already finished. Minimal masking — only at junction line. ~3 min per window. Conditional on casing being already finished.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Light tape at junction. No gaps.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Light tape at junction. Verified seal.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Precision tape at junction. No gaps. Verified.

task_production_rates.name: Adjacent Siding Masking (Spray Only)

S.notes: Small window perimeter masking on siding.

L.notes: Large window — extended siding perimeter to mask.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Paper and tape masking on finished siding around window perimeter to prevent overspray. Only for spray application. Brush has minimal overspray — no siding masking needed.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full perimeter masking. Secured against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full perimeter masking. Tape sealed. No gaps.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full perimeter masking. Taped and sealed. Verified.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Stage brushes (2-inch angular sash primary, 1.5-inch for muntins), paint pots, materials. Set up access equipment per access_type. ~15 min per project setup. Not per-window — fixed time per mobilization.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Materials staged. Access equipment stable.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Materials staged and pre-mixed. Fresh brushes.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Materials mixed and strained. Premium brushes staged.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Configure airless sprayer with 211 tip (0.011 inch orifice, 4-inch fan for window precision). Install 200-mesh filter. Stage 2-inch angular sash brush for back-brushing. Test spray pattern on cardboard. ~30 min per project setup. Not per-window.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern verified.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern at correct distance. Backup tips staged.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Equipment calibrated. Multiple test patterns. Backup tips and filters staged.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Wood Window Surfaces

QT3.notes: Small window full sand 120-150 grit. Even scratch pattern.

QT4.notes: Systematic sand. Inspect all sash edges.

QT5.notes: Raking light inspection. All surfaces including end-grain.

QT4.notes: Systematic sand with profile inspection. ~0.43 hrs.

QT5.notes: Full systematic sand with raking light. ~0.58 hrs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Hand-sand all wood window surfaces (frame, sash rails/stiles, muntins if TDL/SDL) with 120-150 grit to remove mill glaze. Hand-sand only — no orbital sander near glass. Sand WITH grain. Research: 0.30-0.60 hrs/EA for medium window prep. Size bucket scales proportionally.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even scratch pattern. Mill glaze removed. No glossy patches.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full surface sand. No missed areas. Edges and profiles reached.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Systematic sand with raking light. All surfaces including muntin edges and end-grain.

task_production_rates.name: Scuff Sand Factory-Primed Wood Window

S.notes: Light 180-220 grit degloss on small factory-primed wood window.

M.notes: Light degloss on medium window. ~0.20 hrs.

L.notes: Light degloss on large window. ~0.30 hrs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Light scuff-sand factory primer with 180-220 grit to create adhesion profile for topcoat. Factory primer on wood is generally adequate base. Less time than bare wood sanding — no mill glaze removal needed.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Light scuff. Gloss broken on all surfaces.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform scuff. No glossy patches remaining.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Systematic scuff. All surfaces including narrow profiles addressed.

task_production_rates.name: Fill Wood Window Defects

QT4.notes: Fill all defects > 1/16 inch. Sand flush. Raking light verify.

QT5.notes: Fill ALL defects > 1/32 inch. Perfect flush. Raking light.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fill nail holes, minor defects, small damage with exterior-rated wood filler. Cure, sand flush 150-220 grit. Rates shown for medium window. Scale proportionally for S (0.7x) and L (1.5x). For extensive rot: separate scope — flag for estimator.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visible defects filled. Flush to touch.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects > 1/16 inch filled. Sand flush. Raking light verify.
defect_tolerance.QT5: ALL defects > 1/32 inch filled. Perfect flush. Raking light verification.

QT3.notes: Spot prime visible knots. Complete seal.

QT4.notes: Spot prime all knots. Extended coverage around knot area.

QT5.notes: Spot prime all knots with extended perimeter. Verify seal after drying.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply alkyd/shellac stain-blocking primer to visible knots on tannin-rich wood (cedar, redwood, fir). Per-knot application before full acrylic primer. Rates for medium window. Windows have fewer knots than doors/siding due to smaller frame members. Conditional on tannin-rich species.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visible knots sealed. No bleed-through after dry.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All knots sealed including small ones. No bleed-through.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All knots sealed with extended perimeter. Verified seal. Zero bleed-through.

task_production_rates.name: Dust Removal After Sanding (Wood)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth all wood window surfaces after sanding. ~4 min per medium window. Critical for adhesion. Quick task — scale proportionally for S (3 min) and L (6 min).

defect_tolerance.QT3: All surfaces tack-clothed. No visible dust.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All surfaces including profiles tack-clothed. No dust under raking light.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete tack-cloth. White-glove test. Zero contamination.

task_production_rates.name: TSP Wash Aluminum-Clad Window

M.notes: Medium window TSP wash + rinse + dry. ~0.20 hrs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean aluminum-clad surfaces with TSP/TSP-substitute to remove oxidation, chalking, dirt. Rinse thoroughly. Dry completely before scuff-sanding. Includes drying wait allocation.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Surfaces clean. No residue. Dry before sanding.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Surfaces clean. No residue. Fully dry. Inspected.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Surfaces clean. White rag verification. Fully dry.

task_production_rates.name: Scuff-Sand Aluminum-Clad Window

QT5.notes: Full systematic with raking light. Zero glossy spots.
Raking light inspection. Zero glossy spots. ~0.67 hrs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Scuff-sand entire aluminum-clad surface with 180-220 grit for mechanical bonding profile. Hand-sand all surfaces including narrow sash profiles. Aluminum is nonporous — without profile, primer will not adhere. Research: 0.40-0.75 hrs/EA for medium aluminum prep (includes wash + sand). Scuff-sand is the majority of aluminum prep time.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full surface scuff-sand. Even scratch pattern. No glossy patches.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full systematic scuff-sand. All surfaces including narrow profiles.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full systematic with raking light. Zero glossy spots. All profiles addressed.

task_production_rates.name: Dust Removal After Sanding (Aluminum-Clad)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth all aluminum-clad surfaces after scuff-sanding. ~4 min per medium window. Required before corrosion-inhibiting primer application.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All surfaces tack-clothed. No visible dust.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All surfaces tack-clothed. No dust under inspection.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete tack-cloth. Zero contamination.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Vinyl-Clad Window

M.notes: Medium vinyl-clad clean + rinse + dry. ~0.17 hrs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean vinyl-clad with TSP-substitute. NO SANDING — vinyl does not benefit from abrasion. Rinse thoroughly. Dry completely. Fastest prep of the three cladding types. Research: 0.15-0.30 hrs/EA.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full surface clean. No residue.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full surface clean. Fully dry. Inspected for contaminants.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full surface clean. White rag verification. Fully dry.

QT4.notes: Extra pass on end-grain. Raking light inspect.

QT3.notes: Medium wood window brush prime. ~0.50 hrs.

QT5.notes: Full coverage. DFT. Raking light. ~1.25 hrs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush apply 100% acrylic exterior primer to all bare wood surfaces. 2-inch angular sash brush. Horizontal rails first, vertical stiles with grain. Seal all end-grain on sash edges. Research: brush prime is comparable to finish coat time for casement baseline.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage. Seal end-grain. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full even coverage. Extra pass on end-grain. No holidays under raking light.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full even coverage. Extra end-grain. Raking light. DFT-appropriate film.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Apply Acrylic Primer — Wood Window

QT3.notes: Spray + back-brush small wood window. ~0.25 hrs.
Spray + back-brush medium wood window. ~0.37 hrs.

QT5.notes: Precision spray + back-brush. Raking light. ~0.58 hrs.

QT3.notes: Spray + back-brush large wood window. ~0.58 hrs.

QT5.notes: Precision spray + back-brush. Raking light. ~0.92 hrs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray acrylic primer using 211 tip. Back-brush all sash profiles and end-grain. Spray is ~25-30% faster than brush for primer but requires back-brushing on detailed profiles. Spray rate MUST be <= back-brush rate per coupling rule — spray savings come from flat frame areas only.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full spray coverage. Back-brush all profiles and end-grain.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even spray. Back-brush all profiles. Inspect for runs and sags.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Precision spray. Back-brush all profiles. Raking light inspection.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Apply Corrosion-Inhibiting Primer — Aluminum-Clad

QT4.notes: Verify no missed areas on narrow profiles.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush corrosion-inhibiting primer over scuff-sanded bonding profile. MANDATORY even over factory finish. Same application rate as wood primer — slick aluminum surface does not materially affect brush time once bonding profile is established.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage over scuff-sanded surface. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full even coverage. No missed areas on narrow profiles.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full even coverage. Raking light. All profiles addressed.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Apply Corrosion-Inhibiting Primer — Aluminum-Clad
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray corrosion-inhibiting primer using 211 tip. Back-brush narrow sash profiles. MANDATORY even over factory finish. Spray rate <= back-brush rate per coupling rule.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full spray coverage. Back-brush profiles.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even spray. Back-brush all profiles. Inspect for runs.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Precision spray. Back-brush all profiles. Raking light inspection.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage. Schedule topcoat within 1 week.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full even coverage. No holidays. Topcoat < 1 week.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full even coverage. Raking light. Topcoat schedule coordinated.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray PVC bonding primer using 211 tip. Back-brush profiles. MANDATORY for vinyl adhesion. Recoat within 1 week. Spray rate <= back-brush rate per coupling rule.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Even spray. Back-brush all profiles. Topcoat < 1 week.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Precision spray. Back-brush all profiles. Raking light. Topcoat coordinated.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Return sashes to nearly closed position leaving 1-inch gap top and bottom. Prevents paint pooling at closed joints while allowing air circulation. Quick task — ~2 min per window.

factor_modifiers.description: Window type production rate modifier — PRIMARY cost driver alongside size bucket. Applied to finish coat, prime coat, and prep tasks. Does NOT apply to fixed-time tasks (equipment setup, glass masking, sill/casing protection).
factor_modifiers.application_rule: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. Fixed (0.50) = fastest. Bow (2.50) = slowest. Double_hung (1.00) is calibration baseline for M size bucket.
factor_modifiers.notes: User-specified values. Casement is slightly below double-hung baseline. Bay/bow are multi-sash assemblies with proportionally higher time. Fixed is simplest (frame only, no sash hardware or blocking prevention).

factor_modifiers.description: Muntin/grille type modifier for masking and painting labor. Applied to masking setup/teardown and muntin detail tasks.
factor_modifiers.application_rule: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. GBG (grilles between glass) has no painting impact (1.00). SDL adds moderate time (1.25). TDL adds major time (1.75) — individual pane masking + muntin bar painting.
factor_modifiers.notes: User-specified values. TDL range is 1.50-2.00 depending on lite count; 1.75 is midpoint.

factor_modifiers.description: Cladding type prep labor modifier. Applied to prep tasks only — prime and finish rates are consistent across cladding types (same brush/spray technique).
factor_modifiers.application_rule: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. Wood (1.00) = baseline. Aluminum-clad (1.15) = more time due to mandatory scuff-sand. Vinyl-clad (0.90) = less time (clean only, no sanding).
factor_modifiers.notes: User-specified values. Cladding prep is a task-structure branch (different tasks activate), but within each task, this modifier adjusts the base rate.

factor_modifiers.description: Exterior access/height modifier — MAJOR modifier for windows. Applied to ALL labor tasks. Windows are frequently at elevated positions unlike doors (ground level).
factor_modifiers.application_rule: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. Ground (1.00) = baseline. Ladder (1.35) = 35% time increase for second-story. Scaffold (1.60) = 60% time increase for third-story/complex access.
factor_modifiers.notes: Per agent prompt: FAC_EXT_ACCESS (not FAC_HEIGHT) for exterior elevation work. User-specified values. Research suggested ground 1.00, ladder 1.20, scaffold 1.43 — but agent prompt mandates ground 1.00, ladder 1.35, scaffold 1.60 per standard exterior access modifier.

factor_modifiers.description: Quality tier rate modifier. Applied via qt_rates structure on qt_scaled tasks. This modifier captures ADDITIONAL overhead beyond what qt_rates encode directly.
factor_modifiers.application_rule: Already encoded in qt_rates for most tasks. This factor captures additional scrutiny overhead on binary tasks that do not have qt_rates.
factor_modifiers.notes: User-specified values. QT effects are primarily embedded in the qt_rates structure. This modifier is for binary tasks where QT affects pace but a full qt_rates breakdown is not warranted.

factor_modifiers.description: Wind condition modifier. Spray operations blocked at high wind (SOP constraint). Brush operations tolerate wind. Included per agent prompt requirement for exterior specs.
factor_modifiers.application_rule: High wind blocks spray operations entirely. Moderate wind adds ~10% time. Brush operations are unaffected.
factor_modifiers.notes: Research excluded wind from estimation modifiers (unpredictable at bid time). Included here per agent prompt mandatory exterior factor requirement. Engine treats as SOP-level constraint rather than rate modifier.

factor_modifiers.description: Sun exposure modifier. Full sun forces early scheduling, reduces daily productive hours. Included per agent prompt requirement.
factor_modifiers.application_rule: Full sun on south/west elevation = 15% time increase. Per doctrine: 'follow the sun' — paint in shade to prevent temperature blisters.
factor_modifiers.notes: Included per agent prompt mandatory exterior factor. Research excluded from estimation (SOP concern). Primarily affects scheduling rather than per-window rate.

factor_modifiers.description: Surface temperature modifier. Cold/hot extend recoat intervals. Included per agent prompt requirement.
factor_modifiers.application_rule: Cold/hot = 10% time increase (longer recoat waits). Extreme (below 40F or above 95F surface temp) blocks application entirely.
factor_modifiers.notes: Included per agent prompt mandatory exterior factor. Research excluded from estimation. Primarily affects recoat scheduling.

factor_modifiers.description: Substrate condition modifier for prep task rate scaling. NC windows arrive in good condition — minimal impact.
factor_modifiers.application_rule: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. NC windows are typically 'good' condition. 'Fair' for windows with transport damage. 'Poor' is unusual for NC — flag for estimator.
factor_modifiers.notes: Included per agent prompt mandatory exterior factor (FAC_EXT_SUBSTRATE_CONDITION). NC scope means most windows arrive in good condition.

quality_effects.description: Quality tier effects are embedded directly in qt_rates for qt_scaled tasks. Higher QT = slower pace, tighter tolerances, more thorough inspection. QT3: production pace, 6-foot inspection. QT4: slower pace, 3-foot raking light. QT5: meticulous pace, arm's length critical inspection.
quality_effects.mechanism: Rate per tier provided in each qt_scaled task's qt_rates or size_bucket_rates structure.

quality_effects.description: Intercoat sanding is QT4/QT5 only (qt_conditional). QT3 gets visual inspection only. QT4: 220-grit light scuff. QT5: 220 + 320 grit two-pass.
DFT (dry film thickness) verification is QT5 only. Applied during final inspection and intercoat inspection.

assumptions.value: Base rates calibrated to casement window type at each size bucket: S ~25-35 min/coat, M ~45-60 min/coat, L ~75-95 min/coat (brush, QT3-QT5 range)
assumptions.note: Research confirmed: casement 0.5-1.0 hrs/coat. Size buckets scale proportionally. Window type modifier adjusts from casement baseline.

assumptions.value: Spray is only ~25-30% faster than brush for windows due to mandatory back-brushing on detailed profiles
assumptions.note: Windows have high detail-to-field ratio. Back-brushing profiles negates most spray speed advantage. Spray/backroll coupling rule enforced.

assumptions.value: Glass masking teardown is approximately 60-70% of setup time
assumptions.note: No doctrine on masking teardown ratios. Derived from professional practice — film peels quickly, scoring is the time-consuming step.

assumptions.value: NC windows have minimal defects requiring spot repair. Touch-up and spot repair rates reflect low defect incidence.
assumptions.note: New construction windows arrive in good condition. Spot repair and touch-up rates are appropriately low.

assumptions.value: Using FAC_EXT_ACCESS values from agent prompt (ground 1.00, ladder 1.35, scaffold 1.60) rather than research values (1.00, 1.20, 1.43)
assumptions.note: Agent prompt specifies canonical FAC_EXT_ACCESS values. Research values are close but agent prompt is authoritative.

risks.description: TDL masking time is highly variable based on lite count. A 12-lite TDL window takes ~3x longer to mask than a 4-lite TDL.
risks.mitigation: FAC_XWIN_MUNTIN modifier (1.75) is a midpoint. Engine should allow per-window adjustment. Lite count as optional input could improve accuracy.

risks.description: Bay/bow windows have unique structural frames. Production time varies significantly based on configuration (3-sash bay vs 5-sash bow).
risks.mitigation: FAC_XWIN_WINDOW_TYPE values (bay 2.00, bow 2.50) are averages. Field calibration required for specific configurations.

risks.description: Height modifier (FAC_EXT_ACCESS) applies uniformly to all tasks, but some tasks (equipment setup) occur at ground level even for elevated windows.
risks.mitigation: Fixed-time equipment setup tasks are not significantly affected. The modifier primarily impacts per-window production tasks at elevation.

risks.description: PVC bonding primer on vinyl-clad has a strict 1-week topcoat window. Schedule disruptions could require re-priming.
risks.mitigation: SOP Librarian notes capture this constraint. Estimation includes standard primer rate — re-prime is a change order scenario.

validation_plan.description: Time a standard casement (M) brush finish coat start-to-finish. Compare to 35 min QT3 baseline.
Time TDL masking (tape+film) on a 6-lite medium window. Compare to 30 min baseline.
Time double-hung sash sequence (reversal + dry posture + periodic movement + lubrication). Compare to 19 min total.
Compare aluminum-clad prep time (wash + scuff-sand + dust) to wood prep time (sand + fill + dust + tannin spot). Validate aluminum is ~15% more labor.
Time spray+back-brush vs brush-only for same medium casement window. Validate spray is ~25-30% faster.
Time complete window (setup through cleanup) for medium double-hung at QT3 with 1P+2F round. Compare to total derived from task sum.
